subject: Private deploy DPA: BYOK custody, operator read-access, and transfer assurances
messages:
From: Maya R. Singh <maya.singh@medicorps.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on BYOK custody + operator read-access for private deploy
Attachments: MediCorps_DPA_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with line items)

Karthik, Lauren —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare our legal & security package for procurement, a few items in the DPA need concrete answers from Redwood for our internal auditors. I grouped these into the attached spreadsheet but the key asks are below:

1) BYOK custody model: we need a short clause that says Redwood will not have unescorted access to customer CMKs. Can you confirm operator access model (e.g., split custodianship, HSM-backed CMKs, break-glass procedures) and point us to an evidence bundle we can include with the DPA?

2) Operator read-access: will Redwood engineers ever be able to decrypt customer content using support tooling or emergency procedures? If so, under what strict conditions (warrantied break-glass, two-person auth, logged with immutable proofs)?

3) Subprocessors & transfers: for a private VPC deployment in our US region, will any subprocessors outside the US touch logs or telemetry derived from customer input? We need confirmation or a proposed redline for the DPA annex on geofencing and telemetry minimization.

4) Audit artifacts: list of evidence (SOC2 control IDs, sample audit logs, KMS rotation records, attestation letter) you can provide.

We'd like a short written response we can attach to the legal packet by EOD Tuesday PDT. Happy to schedule a 30m call if that helps.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Lead, Privacy & Risk — MediCorps Health
Maya.Singh@medicorps.com

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example>
To: Maya R. Singh <maya.singh@medicorps.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on BYOK custody + operator read-access for private deploy

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet — that's very helpful. Short answers up front, followed by proposed next steps:

- BYOK custody: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) for private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Customers retain the CMK material in their HSM or cloud KMS; Redwood does not store plaintext key material. We can propose DPA language that codifies no unilateral access by Redwood operators and requires documented break-glass procedures.

- Operator read-access: Under our standard private-deploy model, engineers do not have routine decryption abilities of customer content. Emergency access is possible only via an approved break-glass workflow (two approvers, time-limited, audited). We can provide the access workflow and an anonymized sample of logged approvals.

- Subprocessors & transfers: For dedicated private deployments regionally provisioned in the US, we do not route telemetry outside the region except for optional managed support endpoints — which we can disable. We'll propose a DPA annex that restricts telemetry egress to US-located subprocessors unless explicitly consented.

- Audit artifacts: we can assemble a short evidence bundle: SOC 2 summary, redacted KMS rotation events, operator access log sample, and a signed attestation confirming the BYOK model.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll loop in Security (Irene) and Legal (Lauren) to draft redline text for the DPA annex and the operator-access clause.
2) We can attach a 1-page evidence letter + the artifacts you requested.
3) If you want, I'll schedule a 30-minute call Monday or Tuesday to walk through the annex.

Link: https://drive.redwood.company/teams/security/byok-whitepaper — this has our BYOK design + support workflow (internal doc we can share as an evidence artifact).

I'll follow up shortly with the draft language.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.example

Maya / Alan —

Thanks for your patience while we coordinated internally. Attached are two items we can include in your procurement packet: a proposed DPA annex (PDF, redline) and an evidence matrix that lists artifacts we can provide. Summary of key commitments in plain language: 

1) Custody & cryptographic control: For private VPC/on-prem deployments using BYOK, the customer retains sole control of CMK material. Redwood will not possess or persist unencrypted customer key material. Operational actions that would enable decryption (e.g., importing key material into Redwood-managed HSMs) require explicit, documented customer approval.

2) Operator access & emergency procedures: Redwood operators have no routine decryption capability. Emergency investigator access is supported under a break-glass process that requires:
   - documented customer authorization or legal compulsion,
   - endorsement by two named internal approvers (Security + Legal),
   - time-limited, single-use credentials, and
   - release of all approval records and audit logs to the customer within 24 hours of closure.

3) Telemetry & subprocessors: For this deployment we commit to geofenced telemetry handling: telemetry and derived logs will not be exported to subprocessors outside the US without prior written consent. Managed support endpoints that could enable cross-region support will be disabled unless explicitly enabled by the customer.

4) Evidence bundle: We can provide a redacted audit bundle: SOC 2 control summary, sample KMS rotation events (redacted timestamps), anonymized operator approval log (showing the break-glass workflow and approver IDs), and a one-page attestation letter signed by Redwood Security. The attachments indicate which rows we can safely disclose.

If this aligns with MediCorps' needs, Lauren has suggested two small legal edits (minor clarifications around data residency definitions and a short carveout for legal compulsion). Irene has confirmed the availability of the redacted logs we referenced.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Tuesday 10:00 AM PT to walk the annex and evidence bundle together. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
